newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch can't confirm reported Fokker-Samsung deal.
newsitem.headline: Dutch can't confirm reported Fokker-Samsung deal.

text.p: Dutch television news said on Sunday negotiators from Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries had reached broad agreement on a takeover of bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker NV.

But a government spokesman said he was not aware of any such agreement. "There is no memorandum of understanding in preparation at this moment," Ministry of Economic Affairs spokesman Luuc van Zijp said.
Asked if the television report was accurate, Van Zijp said: "I don't think so, unless the NOS news knows more than we do."

Dutch NOS television news said the Samsung negotiators, the Dutch government and administrators appointed to run the bankrupt company had set out broad terms for a takeover of Fokker in a memorandum of understanding drawn up on Friday.
Samsung's senior management was expected to decide by Tuesday whether to approve these terms and if they did, a final agreement was expected by this coming Friday, it said.
The television broadcast did not include any direct comment from representatives of Samsung Aerospace, the Dutch government, or Fokker's administrators.
Fokker was declared bankrupt on March 15 after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospacecut off financial aid, saying it was no longer able to bear Fokker's huge losses.
Since then Samsung Aerospace has emerged as the only serious candidate to revive Fokker's core plane-making operations.
In September the administrators gave Samsung the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books with a view to a possible takeover bid.
